transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

I start out really motivated, but I keep zoning out when people explain what to do and end up not finishing my class assignments or business tasks the way they were asked. It's just getting really frustrating because I'm falling behind in my community college classes and can't seem to get my online shop off the ground.
Do you also find yourself being unusually restless, fidgety, interrupting others, or acting before thinking, or is it mainly trouble paying attention and finishing tasks?

Yes, I definitely experience all of that—I'm constantly jiggling my leg, tapping my fingers, and popping out of my seat during class because sitting still feels physically uncomfortable. I also feel this restless pressure inside and constantly catch myself blurting out answers or finishing people's sentences because I get so impatient. It's a huge part of my daily struggle.
Did these attention and restlessness symptoms start before age 12, and were they present in more than one setting such as school, home, or work?

Yes, they definitely started way before I was 12, both at school and at home. In elementary school, my teachers always wrote comments about me getting out of my seat, talking over other kids, and rushing through projects without finishing. At home, my parents used to joke that I was like a wind-up toy that never stopped moving.
Have these attention, restlessness, or impulsive symptoms been causing clear problems in your daily life, like school/work performance, relationships, or managing responsibilities?

Yes, they are causing major problems for me. I've already failed a required accounting class, had to drop other courses, and am falling way behind on my school plans. Plus, I'm losing money on my online shop because of half-finished inventory and late shipments, which has completely stalled my business.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient meets criteria for ADHD, combined presentation: longstanding symptoms since childhood, present in multiple settings, with both inattention (zoning out, not finishing assignments/tasks) and hyperactivity/impulsivity (fidgeting, inability to stay seated, blurting out answers, interrupting). Symptoms are causing clear academic and occupational/functional impairment.
